newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 12.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 12.2 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading fell during the holiday week of December 23-27 to an average of 12.2 percent of its average daily volume of 254.0 million shares, or 30.9 million shares.
Program trading accounted for an average of 21.6 percent of average daily volume of 529.5 million shares, or 114.4 million shares a day for the week of December 16-20.
Of the average 30.9 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 18.0 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 12.9 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 44.45 million shares a day during the week of December 23-27.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, Susquehanna Brokerage Services and Morgan Stanley executed most of their activity for customers. Nomura Securiies and Lehman Brothers executed most of their activity for their own account.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 65.9 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 32.8 percent of program volume from December 23-27.

Between December 23 and December 27, 27.8 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 2.0 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
